Hi Alice — thanks for the screenshot and the note. This is a sadly-common Google Calendar quirk: when an .ics is forwarded or edited and the VTIMEZONE block is stripped (or the DTSTART/DTEND are expressed without TZID), Calendar will import the times as "floating" and anchor them to the recipient's default zone. That explains why the 19:00 CEST expectation became 09:00 for you.

I've regenerated the invite with an explicit VTIMEZONE block and UTC equivalents included — attaching invite-fixed.ics. A couple of quick options so we avoid confusion:

- If you can accept the attached invite-fixed.ics it should appear at 7:00 PM CEST for you.
- Alternatively, we can anchor the event in UTC in the invite description (e.g., 2027-05-26 19:00 CEST / 17:00 UTC) and ask attendees to add via the Calendar "Add by URL" flow.

I'll hold the slot tentatively for Wed May 26 19:00 CEST. If that doesn't work for anyone, Ben can propose a new time.

Attachments: invite-fixed.ics (text/calendar)

Thanks — sorry for the friction. We run into this occasionally when prospects forward internally across regions.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
